A hot water extract of Jakyak-gamcho-tang (JGT) was manufactured and supplied by KOC Biotech Co. (Daejeon, Republic of Korea). In brief, dried Paeoniae radix (450 g) and Glycyrrhizae radix et rhizoma (450 g) at 1:1 weight ratio were pulverized and subjected to extraction in a hot distilled water (9 L) for 3 h in a reflux extraction system (MS-DM609, MTOPS, Seoul, Republic of Korea). The extract solution was filtered through a 53 micrometer mesh filter, concentrated in a rotary evaporator (Ev-1020, SciLab, Seoul, Republic of Korea) and then lyophilized in a LP-20 freeze dryer (Ilshin-Bio-Base, Dongduchen, Republic of Korea) to get a final JGT extract (219.9 g, 24.4 % yield). The JGT extract was finely homogenized and packed in a foil ziplock bag containing desiccant silica gels. For in vitro studies, homogenous JGT (100 mg) was vigorously voltexed for 30 min at room temperature in a 10 mL phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Rockford, IL, USA) containing 2% DMSO and then sterilized by filtering through a 0.22 micrometer membrane to get a JGT stock solution (10 mg/mL). The JGT stock solution was aliquoted in a small volume and stored at -80°C until used. For RNA extraction, first, a JGT concentration exhibiting 80% cell viability in myotubes was calculated using a 4-parameter logistic curve fit and determined to be 500 microgr/mL as the maximum tolerable dose for RNA sequencing analysis. Then, C2C12 myoblasts were differentiated for 6 days on 6-well culture plates and then treated with increasing doses of JGT (20, 100, and 500 microgr/mL) for 24 h. A vehicle control was treated with 0.1% DMSO. After 24-h treatment, total RNA was extracted.

A C2C12 murine myoblast cell (CRL-1772) was purchased from American Type Culture Collection (Manassas, VA, USA) and maintained in a growth medium (GM, Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium with 4.5 gr/L glucose (DMEM) supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum, 100 I.U penicillin and 100 microgr/mL streptomycin at 37°C in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator. For differentiation to myotubes, GM was replaced with differentiation medium (DM, DMEM supplemented with 2% heat-inactivated horse serum, 100 I.U penicillin and 100 microgr/mL streptomycin) when myoblasts were grown to 80-90% confluence. The DM was replaced with a fresh one every 2 days for total 5-7 days. A basal medium and supplements used for C2C12 cell culture were purchased from Thermo Fisher Scientific.
